data.narrative:
Seasats is a Series A-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Mike Flanigan, Dan Flanigan, Dylan Rodriguez, and Max Kramers. The company has raised approximately $40M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of two private-stage companies in the ocean and maritime sector—Bedrock Ocean and Havoc AI—given the absence of directly comparable public comps in this frontier vertical.

Stage-progression methodology, the primary applicable triangulation approach, uses the $40M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage advancement. This method yields an implied valuation of $80M. The resulting triangulated range spans $68M (low) to $92M (median $80M, high). The 2.0x multiplier reflects normalized step-up scaling for early-stage technology companies progressing through venture capital rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation band of $68M to $92M, centered on $80M. Key limitations include reliance on a single valuation method and a sparse peer set of only two private comparables, which constrains cross-validation and limits confidence in relative positioning. Uncertainty around Seasats' revenue trajectory, unit economics, and competitive positioning within ocean tech remains material. Additional financial and operational metrics would strengthen confidence in this range.
